findings.title: Oracle-based caused-at rule has no reading branch and misattributes several case types
findings.section: Step 3, Surfaced and caused (lines 282-286); Step 2 oracle table, E+R* row (line 176)
findings.problem:
Line 283 maps oracle row results to caused-at: R-hint means key assignment, R-resolver means key resolution, E+R but not R means extraction, and not recovered by E+R* means state rules, transcript or evaluation. Dropping Q (value m0) left this rule with gaps:
(a) Reading. No branch yields reading. Rows that surface at key_reached, in_payload or answered were already stored with the right status in the recorded run, so at the status endpoint they are 'unchanged'. Read literally, they are 'not recovered by E+R*', and the rule sends about 9-11 reading rows per A0/A1 run to state rules, transcript or evaluation.
(b) Missing branches. Some rows are recovered by E+R* but not E+R: a negative carrier outranks the median-confidence injection. Some are recovered by R but by neither R-hint nor R-resolver alone. Neither group has a branch.
(c) E+R* is not 'the state rules' own share' (line 176). It removes only the 0-2 negative carriers of current values per run. It keeps the 3-7 positive carriers of ruled-out values per run that R and E+R move onto those values' own gold keys (feasibility F3), and it keeps the wrong-modality carriers. A ruled-out row re-adopted by one of these is then coded as state rules.
(d) Legitimate rivals. R also removes legitimate same-matter rivals, because non-carriers stay on the system key. In the A2 sample, about 4 of 16 conflicted keys held variants of one matter. Value F3's skeptic concluded that the coding, not R, must separate routing from legitimate rivals. Line 283 now lets R decide mechanically, and the R-limit sentence was dropped.
(e) No default. When neither an oracle result nor page evidence exists, the rule gives no default. Value F5's better_change said 'unclear'. Line 285 says only that caused-at never defaults to the surfacing step.

findings.title: Blind codes cannot match the oracle-set caused-at, and 'agreed codes' is undefined
findings.section: Step 3: Surfaced and caused (lines 283, 288), Case pages (line 309), Coders (lines 313-318), Agreement (lines 321-323); Step 4 eligibility (line 347)
findings.problem:
The class is coded for the caused-at boundary (line 288), and an oracle result sets caused-at mechanically (line 283). But oracle results are not on the page (line 309), and pass 1 and the second coder code blind from the page (lines 313, 315). Their codes are therefore for boundaries the coders chose. Agreement is measured on pass 1 against the second coder (line 322), while the codes that enter Step 4 must be for the oracle's boundary. Five more gaps follow.
- 'Agreed codes' (line 347) does not say which author pass is compared, or how a caused-at disagreement counts.
- The double-coded set is keyed to pass 1 or the model (line 316). A case that pass 2 moves into implementation after seeing the oracle is double-coded only if it falls in the 30% sample.
- 'At least 5 cases per eligible sub-cause' can exceed the sampled cases of a 3-value cause, and cases outside the sample have no author code.
- There is no kappa on caused-at (value F5 item 5).
- After a codebook revision, the draft does not say whether the 180 coded cases are recoded. The binary-kappa lower bound and the D3 carry-over (value F7) are also missing.
findings.proposed_change:
Add a reveal step to Step 3:
"After pass 1 and the second coder's codes are hashed, the oracle caused-at, where one exists, is shown to both coders. Each re-codes the class for that boundary, and the blind and revealed codes are both reported."
Define 'agreed' in Step 4: "the author's pass-2 code and the second coder's revealed code both say implementation defect, with the same primary sub-cause".
Widen the double-coded set to every case that any author pass, the model or the reveal puts in implementation. If an eligible sub-cause has fewer than 5 sampled cases, its further cases are drawn in hash order and coded by both coders.
Report kappa on blind caused-at next to class kappa.
After a revision, recode all sampled cases before measuring the fresh sample.
Report the binary kappa's lower 95% bound. The codes feed D3's 'affected' rule only if that bound is at least 0.40; otherwise the shortfall is reported as a limit of the dry run.
State that the registration carries the binary measure, and the double-coding of implementation cases, over to the confirmatory coding.

findings.title: The prompt test rules out two listed extraction causes and contradicts the burden rule and the probe readings
findings.section: Step 3 classes (line 266); class rules, Burden (line 274); candidate causes (line 294); Step 2b result meaning (line 225)
findings.proposed_change:

"A prompt counts when (i) it omits information the register gives that step; (ii) it contradicts the register; or (iii) a design-neutral change to its composition, fixed in the Step 2b note, recovers the case under the probe recovery rule. Such changes are a registry cut by the resolver's own rule, or neutral examples. A rewording argued only on the case page does not count. A parameter counts when the trace shows it excluded the right item."

findings.title: Model-limited and the probe readings have no recovery criterion, and no rule where no probe exists
findings.section: Step 2b (lines 211-228); Step 3 classes, Model-limited (line 271); Rules fixed (line 389)
findings.problem:
The probe rules leave four gaps.
- 'Recovered ... beyond the noise control' is undefined. Only the probe conditions are fixed before the calls, not the recovery criterion.
- (d) gets one repeat against a three-repeat noise control, so a single gpt-5.4 success cannot be told apart from sampling noise. No code exists for cases the recorded prompt itself recovers on repeat (value F1's 'sampling instability').
- Model-limited is assignable only when (d) recovers. But (d) covers only A0/A1 extraction cases, and Step 2b needs its own go-ahead. Routing, reading, A2 and 3b cases can never be model-limited, and neither can any case if 2b is declined. Integrity F2's residual case (the step got everything the design gives it and still erred) therefore falls to architectural weakness. That is the outcome integrity F2's rule (3) was meant to prevent.
- A case recovered under both (c) and (d) fits both 'registry-conditioned' and 'model-limited'.
findings.proposed_change:
In Step 2b, fixed now:
- "A condition recovers a case when it carries it in at least 2 of 3 repeats and (a) carries it in at most 1 of 3."
- "(d) gets three repeats, about $10 more."
- "Cases that (a) carries in 2 or 3 of 3 repeats get the sub-cause 'sampling instability', coded implementation or unclear, never design."
In the class table, add: "Where no probe exists (routing, reading, A2, 3b, or 2b declined), a case is coded 'model-limited, unprobed' when its step received everything the register gives it, no parameter excluded the right item, and the transcript is not difficult. It is reported separately and never as architecture."
Code a recovery under both (c) and (d) as registry-conditioned, with the model as a contributing cause.
Add the recovery criterion to Rules fixed.

findings.title: Retrospective design text still licenses architectural codes, including A2's open conflicts
findings.section: Step 0 register (line 80); Step 3 classes (lines 267-268); Burden rule (line 274); Decisions needed
findings.problem:
The register marks D10, D11 and 'the autonomous arm leaves conflicts open' as retrospective, written after cycle 1. That mark constrains only the trade-off class. Architectural weakness is 'the loss follows from a design decision of the register', with no restriction. The burden rule also lets an alternative be ruled out by 'which design decision it would contradict', so a retrospective decision can exclude an alternative and yield an architectural code.
A2 shows the effect. Its 36.7 rows per run of open same-meeting conflicts follow from the retrospective conflicts-open sentence, so they can be coded architectural while 'who resolves conflicts' is formally open. The draft says only that they are not a trade-off. It neither says how they are coded until the decision nor schedules that decision before the A2 cases are coded, and the decision is not in 'Decisions needed'. Integrity F2's better_change (4) and (5) are not adopted.
findings.proposed_change:
Add to the class rules:
- "An architectural code, or a burden-rule exclusion, that rests on a retrospective entry (D10, D11, the conflicts-open sentence) must also cite the same choice in D1-D9 as documented at 94c049d, or in code that predates the cycle-1 runs. Otherwise the case is unclear."
- "A2 open-conflict cases are coded 'pending: conflict decision' until the Step 0 open decision is signed. The decision is taken before any A2 case code is read."
Add that decision to 'Decisions needed'.

findings.title: LLM-seam repairs, and D1, are still accepted on 'fewer losses' over 3 against 3 runs
findings.section: Step 4 (b), Checking a repair (line 359); Step 2c (lines 236-239)
findings.problem: This is unchanged from round 1, although integrity F7 and value F8 both gave fixed criteria. Within one arm, run-to-run spread at a boundary is 11-13 rows: filing 21-34 in A1, extraction 39-52 in A0. Any mean difference over 3 against 3 runs is inside that noise. A repair with no effect can therefore be accepted and counted as 'repaired', which states the wrong end state for its losses. Step 2c's 'fewer extraction losses' and 'no rise in filing losses' have the same problem.
findings.proposed_change:
Line 359:
"Prediction: the A1′ mean loss at the boundary is at least 5 rows and 3 distinct values below the same-period A1 mean, every A1′ run is below every A1 run (exact one-sided p = 1/20), and there is no new incidence. Otherwise the result is 'not shown': the switch stays off and the cause is an unrepaired implementation defect."
Apply the same criterion to Step 2c's direction. State D1's harm check as "mean filing losses not higher by more than 5 rows".

findings.title: D1's result has no route into the coding or into Step 5, and Step 5 lacks the A1 reference arm
findings.section: Step 2c; Step 3 classes and burden rule; Step 5 Arms (line 375)
findings.problem:
Step 2c runs D1, but four gaps remain.
- No codebook rule says how its result bears on the `carried:claims_without_the_value` cases (integrity F11 (c)). Read under the burden rule as an in-design alternative, D1 makes those cases implementation defects. Read as a design alternative, which plan 23 treats it as, it makes them architectural, with D1 as evidence. The coder decides.
- Step 5's arms are 'A0 and the final candidate'. If the final candidate includes D1, an A2 contract or A1′, ES2009 has no A1 baseline, so the contract verdicts lack the on/off contrast plan 23 D3 uses. The draft also does not say that an accepted A1′ replaces A1 as the reference arm (integrity F7, F11 (d)).
- D1 is compared with the A1 runs of 22-23 October, while Step 4 requires same-period A1 controls for any LLM-seam change.
findings.proposed_change:
Add a codebook rule: "D1 is a Phase C contract, that is, a design alternative. Cases at `carried:claims_without_the_value` are coded architectural weakness (D10, with its pre-cycle-1 citation) and cite the D1 result as evidence. If D1 works, they are reported as recoverable by a design alternative."
Step 5 arms: "A0; A1, or A1′ if accepted, which then replaces A1 as the reference arm; and the final configuration where it differs, meaning any contract whose development verdict is *works* under the rule written before these runs. Three runs each."
Step 2c: add three interleaved same-period A1 runs (about $10). Otherwise label the comparison with the existing A1 runs as different-period and indicative only.

findings.title: A2-only causes are eligible and ordered, but have no way to be checked
findings.section: Step 4 (b): Ordering (line 355) and Checking a repair (lines 358-359)
findings.problem:
A2-only causes are counted for eligibility and ordering, by 'A2 first-loss counts'. But every check procedure runs on A0/A1:
- state-logic repairs on the six recorded A0/A1 runs;
- LLM-seam repairs on A1′ against A1.
The A2 contracts are off in all of these, so an A2-only repair (for example to the support or type check) cannot show fewer losses. It fails by construction and becomes an unrepaired implementation defect. Integrity F1 named A2-only causes as excluded by construction, and they still are, only now through the check rather than the threshold. The A2 harness that Step 2 already builds is not used.
findings.proposed_change:
Add to Checking a repair:
- "A2-only state-logic repairs are checked in the harness, paired on the A2 runs that pass the A2 gate: fewer losses at the boundary in every gated run, and no new incidence."
- "A2-only LLM-seam repairs are checked with three A2′ runs against three same-period A2 runs, under the criterion of Step 4 (about $21)."
Alternatively, state that A2-only causes are not repairable in this round, are reported as unrepaired implementation defects, and leave the contract mechanisms they touch *can't tell*.

findings.title: Oracle R still turns passing no-successor demoted rows into losses
findings.section: Step 2 oracle table (R and E+R rows); Two-sided output (lines 178-187)
findings.problem: Draft 2 adds an asserted negation at the change span for F27, F35 and F56 under E+R only. R injects nothing. Under R these values sit alone on their gold keys and nothing retires them, so the 5 rows (F27@c,d; F35@c,d; F56@d) flip from pass to lost as an artifact of the definition. That lowers R's net recovery, which now feeds caused-at and the repair ordering. Feasibility F3's better_change, to exclude these rows from the R tallies and list them, is not adopted.
findings.proposed_change: Add under the oracle table: "Under R, the five rows F27@c,d, F35@c,d and F56@d are excluded from the tallies and listed with their outcome." Alternatively, apply the same asserted negation at the change span under R.

findings.title: Frozen-input rules conflict with the adjudication audit and omit inputs that later steps use
findings.section: Frozen inputs (lines 48, 72); Adjudication audit (line 325); Step 2c; Step 3 case pages
findings.problem:
Four gaps remain.
- Line 48 says Steps 2-4 use the frozen v1 adjudications, and corrections are reported next to them, never in place of them. Line 325 says that if audit agreement is below 0.80, the oracles are recomputed with the human decisions before Step 4. These rules contradict each other. Neither says which version sets caused-at and the Step 4 ordering, or whether cases whose oracle row result flips are re-coded. Integrity F8's 'qualifies under both v1 and v2' rule is missing.
- Line 48 says Steps 2-4, line 72 says Steps 2-3a. The two disagree on whether the new runs of Steps 2c and 4 use the frozen suite and gold.
- New claim texts from those runs need new adjudications, and the draft has no rule for where they go.
- The EL2020 RAG runs (rag_r1-r3), which feed the case pages and the recoverability rule, are not in the manifest.
findings.proposed_change:
- State that a cause is eligible, and a caused-at is set, only if the result holds under v1 and under any audit-driven v2. Cases whose row result differs between versions are re-coded at the reveal step.
- Make line 72 match line 48: 2c and Step 4 runs are scored on the frozen suite and gold, with post-B3 scores reported beside them.
- New-run adjudications go to a dated file per batch.
- Add the three RAG runs' answer and scorecard hashes to the manifest.

findings.title: Cost and author time are still low, and the budget sentence contradicts the table
findings.section: Step 2b estimate (line 230); Cost and time (lines 409-423)
findings.problem:
- **Step 2b.** A rough estimate puts (i) at about $11-14: about 170 spans × 12 mini calls at 2-9.5k input tokens, plus one gpt-5.4 call each. Probe (d) is only about $5 of that. Probe (ii) adds about $7-12: some 45-70 carriers and rivals per run × 6 runs × 3 repeats, on an unpruned prompt of 40-67k characters at $0.75 per million tokens. The step is therefore about $20-26, not $10-15, and adjudicating the probes' new claim texts is not in its agent time.
- **Step 4.** Each LLM-seam repair costs about $20, and up to four boundaries can each have one. The total assumes one.
- **Total and budget.** A realistic total is about $46-75. Line 423 says the upper end 'would go past' plan 23's $60-100 range, but $32 + $65 = $97 is inside it.
- **Author time.** 245 cases at 3-5 minutes is 12-20 h for pass 1 alone. Pass 2, the pilot, about 72 pass rows (20% of the 361 pass rows in nine runs) plus the credit_without_state questions, and any fresh agreement sample are not counted. 'The next 20 cases' for the pilot is also ambiguous: 20 in all, or 20 per run.
- **Second coder.** The double-coded set plus the adjudication audit likely exceeds 100-120 items.
findings.proposed_change:
- Step 2b: about $20-30 including (d) at three repeats, plus an adjudication round.
- Step 4: about $20 per LLM-seam repair, with the count stated.
- Total: about $45-80.
- Line 423: compute the budget comparison from the corrected total.
- Author time: about 18-30 h, itemised.
- Second coder: about 120-170 cases plus the audit.
- Pilot: "20 cases in all, in global hash order".

findings.title: No copy check on the second coder's file
findings.section: Step 3 Coders and Agreement (lines 315-323)
findings.problem: Integrity F3's better_change item 3 asked for the 19-citation-sample copy check: if the second coder's agreement with the model pre-codes reaches 95%, or clearly exceeds the author's, ask before using the file. Draft 2 leaves it out. The repair-eligibility rule ('agreed codes') and the D3 'can't tell' rule both rest on the second coder being independent. A machine-derived second file would make 'agreed' mean that the author agrees with a model.
findings.proposed_change: Add under Agreement: "Copy check (as in `19-citation-sample`): compute the second coder's agreement with the model pre-codes. If it reaches 95%, or clearly exceeds the author's agreement with the model, the file is not used until the coder has been asked how it was produced."

findings.title: No bound on the harness-fix loop or the adjudication fixpoint, and no Step 4 rule when no oracle exists
findings.section: Step 2 Identity gate (lines 164-166); Two-sided output, Adjudication (lines 181-184); Step 4 Ordering and Checking (lines 348-358)
findings.problem:
- **Harness fixes.** A failed gate is 'fixed and the gate re-run' with no limit. 'If no A0/A1 run passes' therefore has no point at which it is decided (integrity m1).
- **Adjudication.** Oracle results wait until the adjudication queue is empty, with no cap on rounds.
- **No oracle.** Without oracle evidence, Step 4's ordering measures (R-hint, R-resolver, E+R beyond R, the E+R* residual) do not exist, and the draft gives no replacement.
- **Gated runs.** 'Fewer losses in at least 5 of 6 runs' assumes all six A0/A1 runs pass the gate.
findings.proposed_change:
Add:
- "The harness gets at most N fix rounds, or D days of agent work (fixed now). A run still failing after that counts as failed."
- "The adjudication fixpoint is capped at three rounds. Items still open are reported as unresolved and excluded from that oracle's result."
- "Without oracle results, causes are ordered by distinct values from the agreed codes alone."
- "The harness check requires fewer losses in all but at most one of the runs that pass the gate, with at least four gated runs; otherwise the check is not available and the cause is reported as unrepaired."

findings.title: ES2009 3b: which runs are coded, and its double coding, are not fixed; the A2 'home case' rule is missing

- **Run choice.** 3b codes 'one ES2009 A0 run and one run of the final candidate', but does not say which of Step 5's three runs. That leaves the choice to be made after reading, which integrity F5 asked to remove. Its better_change offered a rule such as r1 of each arm, stated now.
- **Double coding.** The draft does not say whether 3b is double-coded, or whether its kappa is reported separately (feasibility F8, value F11).
- **Home case.** Value F11 item 3 is not carried: an A2 result on ES2009 is the contracts' home case, and the verdict rule must say how it counts.

- Fix the run choice now: "3b codes all cases of ES2009 A0 r1 and the final candidate's r1".
- Add: "The second coder codes at least 30% of 3b, drawn within 3b, and 3b's kappa is reported separately."
- Add to Step 5: "If A2 runs on ES2009, the verdict rule states that this is the contracts' home case. A favourable result there does not outweigh EL2020."

findings.title: A0's role in 3a is undefined for defects already repaired in A1
findings.section: Step 3 Sample (lines 251-253); Step 4 eligibility (line 347); Effect on Phase D (line 338)
findings.problem: 3a codes the three A0 runs in full, and eligibility is counted over all of 3a. A0 carries the Phase B bugs: about 33-36 defect-flagged current rows per run. Nothing says that A0 cases coded to a Phase-B bug count as 'repaired' (end state 1), or that they are kept out of eligibility and out of the 'can't tell' sweep. Three values can also come from A0 alone, which makes eligible a cause that A1 may not have. Its A1′ check would then fail, giving a false 'unrepaired' and *can't tell*. Value m1's point is therefore neither adopted nor answered.
findings.proposed_change:
Add:
- "A0 cases whose primary code is a Phase B bug are coded 'repaired (Phase B, switch X)'. They count toward neither eligibility nor 'can't tell'."
- "Eligibility for an implementation-choice repair needs at least one of the 3 values in A1 or A2 runs."
- "A0 codes are also reported as the reflection on cycle 1."

findings.title: 'Any touched mechanism is can't tell' over a 1-in-3 sample makes the verdicts depend on which cases the sample draws
findings.section: Effect on Phase D (line 338); Sample (line 251)
findings.problem: Every mechanism touched by one unrepaired implementation case, or one unclear case, becomes *can't tell*. Coding covers only 20 of about 60 cases per run, and up to 10% of cases may be unclear. Whether a mechanism is 'touched' therefore depends on which cases the hash sample draws, and nearly every mechanism is likely to be touched. A contract then cannot reach *works* and cannot enter the final configuration. Plan 23 D3 leaves the 'affected' rule to be fixed, so the dry run should test a rule that does not depend on the sample. This problem arises from combining integrity F0/value F0's 'touch' rule with integrity F5's sample.
findings.proposed_change:
Define 'touched' through the claims register's mapping from boundaries to mechanisms. Report each mechanism's sample-weighted share of unrepaired, possible-implementation and unclear losses, with its interval, and the model pre-code share on all cases beside it.
State explicitly that the any-touch rule is the dry-run rule, and that the registration chooses between it and a share-based rule.

findings.title: Smaller omissions from adopted better_changes (value F2, F9, F10)
findings.section: Step 2 'A2, offline' (lines 195-202); Step 3 outputs; Case pages
findings.problem:
Value F10:
- The leave-one-out runs over A2's recorded claims can need support verdicts that were never recorded, for example when a claim the type check rejected now reaches the support check. Line 146 makes any such call an error, so the decomposition can halt. The better_change allowed support calls 'for any new winner (a few cents)'.
- The reviewer oracle is not labelled a perfect-reviewer ceiling, and keys mixing several gold values are not counted separately.
Value F9:

- Cases without a single-value question are not marked 'no independent recoverability evidence'.
Value F2:
- Routing-path shares are not reported against each arm's base rate of hint-keyed claims (A0 54-63%, A1 50-55%).

result.overall:
Draft 2 adopts most round-1 reference changes: a replay harness, oracles with no live fallback, E+R and E+R*, two-sided net output, Step 2b probes, Step 2c (D1), a hash sample across all nine runs, two author passes, per-cause eligibility in place of the 10-row threshold, conformance repairs split from implementation-choice ones, three end states, the registers, frozen hashes (verified against the files: all five SHA-256 values match, and a0_r1's manifest prefix dedea0ba reproduces) and the 3a/3b split.

Nine major gaps remain:
- the caused-at rule's gaps, created when Q was dropped and R was made the decider;
- blind coding that conflicts with the oracle-set caused-at;
- blindness that the step order defeats;
- a prompt test that contradicts the burden rule;
- probe-dependent classes with no recovery criterion;
- retrospective design text that still licenses architectural codes;
- a noisy LLM-seam acceptance criterion;
- no route for D1's result, and no A1 arm in Step 5;
- A2-only causes that cannot be checked.

result.reasoning:
I could not refute the finding. Each gap is real in draft 2. Two parts of it are slightly mis-stated, and one part of its proposed fix should not be adopted.

**1. The recovery criterion is undefined.**
- Line 225 says "beyond the noise control", and nothing defines it.
- Line 211 fixes only "prompt variants and parameter values" before any call, and Rules fixed (line 389) lists only "the probe conditions".
- The criterion decides outcomes. Model-limited exists only "when probe (d) recovers" (line 271), and pass 2 joins the probe results (line 314). A threshold picked after the probe results are seen is a forking path in a file whose spine is "rules fixed before any outcome".
- Round 1 proposed this exact rule: value F2's verdict says "at least 2 of 3 repeats and (a) at most 1 of 3", and adds "sampling instability". Draft 2 dropped both.

**2. (d) has one repeat against three for (a), and there is no code for (a)'s own recoveries.**
- This is true as stated (line 218 against line 213).
- One more point makes it worse. If gpt-5.4 rejects temperature 0, the client silently falls back to the default temperature (app/llm/openai_llm.py:143 and 208-209), which adds more noise to a single draw.
- The finding's cost of "about $10 more" is rough. A0/A1 have 152 distinct values lost at extraction over six runs (23-loss-trace.json, strict series), and round 1 counted up to 356 (checkpoint, span) pairs. An extraction call is about 8k input tokens (facts_costs: 1.02M tokens over 127 calls). At gpt-5.4 list price ($2.50/$15) that is about $0.025 a call, so two more repeats cost about $8–18 nominal.

**3. Model-limited cannot be reached outside A0/A1 extraction.**
- This is true. Probe (d) exists only in (i), on the six A0/A1 runs (line 213). Probes (ii) and (iii) have no model condition. A2 and ES2009 (3b) get no probes, and Step 2b needs its own go-ahead (line 204).
- Take a routing case where the resolver had the gold key in its prompt and still chose wrong. Under the burden rule (line 274) that case is coded architectural or unclear, because a stronger model is not an in-design alternative.
- An architectural code licenses "routing is a design limit" (lines 365 and 407). The draft's evidence cannot separate the model from the design here.
- The rule this breaks is item (3) of the round-1 residual rule. In review_result.json that is integrity **F3**'s verdict; the finding calls it "F2", following the digest's order.

**4. The (c)+(d) overlap.**
- The finding says such a case fits both labels. That is inexact. Lines 226–227 ("only under (d)", "only under (c)") give it neither label, while the class table (line 271) gives it model-limited. So the draft contradicts itself rather than double-counts.

**Where the proposed fix goes too far.** The label "model-limited, unprobed" assigns the model by elimination, with no evidence. That is the same defaulting the draft forbids for design (lines 20 and 23: "shown, with evidence"; "No loss becomes a design limit by default"). The honest label for an unprobed residual is "design or model, not separated".

The finding is not refuted. It needs those corrections.

result.overall:
Draft 2 fixes most of what round 1 found. The harness is specified as a replay of the deterministic services, with no live fallback. Losses now end in three states, and the burden rule, achievability probes, surfaced/caused split, 3a/3b order, ES2009 framing and pass sampling are all in. I checked the inputs: the five frozen-input hashes match, and these figures reproduce from 23-loss-trace.json: routing 34-41 rows, extraction about 45, reading 9-11 (key_reached about 7), first-checkpoint extraction loss 27.3/31.4/46.1/47.0%, and 12 of 65 values with a stable first-loss boundary.

Three problems would still let an outcome steer a decision, or let implementation pass as design:
(1) The verdict rule that admits contracts and repairs is written before Step 5. By then the D1 arm, the A2 per-contract decomposition, the reviewer oracle and the Step 4 checks have all been read.
(2) Only the trade-off class is barred from retrospective design text. So D10, written 19 October after cycle 1, can make the largest extraction loss an architectural weakness, and a conflict decision signed after the results can make A2's conflicts a trade-off.
(3) The narrow prompt and parameter tests, the burden rule and the probe-meaning rules contradict each other. Three of the listed candidate causes cannot qualify as implementation under the definition meant to admit them.

Several steps cannot run as written:
- The A2 offline variants need live support checks: only 313 of 534 a2_r1 claims have a recorded verdict.
- Probe (b) barely shrinks the registry: the _prompt_registry rule applied to a span keeps a median 95 of 146 keys.
- Step 4's harness check would replay A0 runs under A1 switches that need unrecorded LLM calls.
- Its '5 of 6 runs' prediction fails by construction whenever a cause occurs in fewer runs.
- The live repair check has no effect size, so noise can label a loss 'repaired'.

Other gaps:
- R-hint/R-resolver attribute a routing loss to the carrier's path when the error is usually the rival's.
- Pass 1 is not blind to the aggregate oracle and probe results.
- The double-coded set and repair eligibility depend on each other.
- RAG with the same model is not used against 'model-limited'.
- Defects that inflate passes are never looked for.
- A single unclear case makes a mechanism can't tell, which will make every development verdict uninformative.

Numbers: author coding is about 12-20 h for one pass of the 245 cases, not two, before the pilot and the pass examinations. The probes cost about $20, not $10-15, because the live routing probe was left out. And $32 plus $65 does not go past $60-100.

Proportionality: cut A0 hand coding, reduce 3b to a transfer check without a second coder, drop the A2 one-on variants, cap the adjudication audit, and test read-path repairs by paired answer replay. Keep the harness with R and E+R, probes (i) and (ii), 3a on A1 and A2, and Step 4.

findings.title: The identity-gate fix loop is open-ended, and the instrument changes are unverified
findings.section: Step 2 identity gate; Step 0 instrument changes
findings.problem:
Each failed gate is fixed and re-run, with no cap on rounds or days. If no run passes, state-logic repairs have no check path, and that is not stated.

findings.title: The reviewer oracle on A2 is a gold-informed bound, not a reviewer
findings.section: Step 2 'Reviewer oracle on A2'
findings.problem: The oracle resolves conflicts to the gold value, which is a ceiling. It cannot show that the conflict contract 'works with a reviewer'. Matching rival values to the gold value also needs the matcher and the adjudication, which is not stated.

findings.title: The burden rule triggers only when the coder names an alternative
findings.section: Step 3 class rules (burden); case pages
findings.problem: If a coder names no in-design alternative, the burden rule is never triggered, and architectural weakness becomes the easy code.
findings.proposed_change: Require each case page to address every listed candidate cause for its caused-at boundary, saying why it would not recover the case. The per-boundary register sheet becomes a checklist.

findings.title: 'Not approved' is an open veto on repairs

findings.problem: An eligible cause can be left unrepaired because it is 'not approved', and no criterion is given. This lets the author choose which mechanisms are tested and which stay can't tell.

The finding holds. One part of it misreads the draft.

Taken literally, that already bars the author from seeing aggregate results before pass 1. Only line 309 ("not on the page") and line 252 ("joined to a case") limit it to per-case joining.

**Why the problem is still real:**
- **Nothing in the draft makes line 313 enforceable.** The steps are numbered 2, 2b, 2c, then 3. The cost table gives the author "review the gates" for Step 2. Step 2c is "contrasted with the three existing A1 runs". Nowhere does the draft schedule pass 1 before those outputs exist, or seal them from the author. As written, the author codes pass 1 after reading the oracle matrices, probe recovery by condition and the D1 arm. All three bear directly on the implementation-versus-design class:
  - (b)/(b2) recovery means implementation choice;
  - (d)-only recovery means model-limited;

The finding largely holds when checked against draft 2 (thesis/notes/thesis_completion/artifacts/23-plan-amendment-1-ceilings-and-root-cause.md) and the round-1 review. Only part (c) is overstated.

(a) The conflict is real, and it comes from merging two round-1 proposals. Round 1 offered two prompt rules. One was narrow: a prompt counts only if it omits or contradicts register information. The other was probe-based: a prompt counts when a design-neutral probe recovers the case (review_digest.md:608/628 against 1256). Draft 2 put the narrow rule in the class table (line 266) and the probe reading in Step 2b (line 225), and never reconciled them.

The recorded extraction prompt carries the full registry and the AMI role examples (app/services/extraction_service.py:202-204). Ch. 4 D4 says claims are matched to existing concepts, so the registry is in scope. Neither the registry nor the examples omits or contradicts register information. So a case recovered under (b) or (b2) cannot pass the line-266 test, yet line 225 calls that recovery evidence for implementation choice.

The burden rule (line 274) allows only two grounds for ruling out an alternative: it would not recover the case, or it contradicts a design decision. Failing the narrower test is not one of them. A coder can therefore argue either way. Two listed extraction candidates (line 294), registry-conditioned extraction and out-of-domain examples, can then never meet the class definition. The draft says these class rules decide outcomes and are frozen, so this is not cosmetic.

(b) The parameter test covers exclusion only ("excluded the right item"). Plan 23:252 and 23-loss-trace-results.md:103 say the routing rivals are mostly different matters on one key. That is over-inclusion. So the listed `expansion_reuse_threshold` candidate (line 296) cannot meet the test.

(c) Overstated. The class table's "Assigned only when (d) recovers and no in-design probe does" is a necessary condition, not a sufficient one. A case recovered under (c) and (d) is therefore permitted, not required, to be model-limited. Step 2b gives such a case no label. That is still a real gap at a boundary that decides outcomes. "Registry-conditioned" maps to no class, and the probe reading (lines 224-228) is missing from "Rules fixed" (lines 383-401).

The unclear rule does not resolve the problem. It applies when a coder cannot judge, and here the conflicting rules let a coder judge confidently either way.

- It cites a "noise rule" that does not exist. Step 2b has only a noise control (a) with no numeric criterion.
- It ignores that probe results are not on the case pages (line 304). Pass 1 and the second coder are both blind to them, so probe-based tests and model-limited can only enter in pass 2. That is better handled mechanically, the way the draft already lets oracle results set caused-at (line 284).
- It does not add "fails the narrower tests" as a ground under the burden rule, which is what actually aligns the two rules.
